title: Gustav II Adolf to Axel Oxenstierna, Stockholm, 18 Nov 1627 (last part), Riksarkivet Chifferklaver låda II:114 (DECODE R4284; from catalogue item 207)

documents.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Chifferklaver låda II:114, DECODE R4284
documents.date: 18 Nov 1627 (from the 1888 print; no dateline on R4284; the day 18 is the editors', from the register; filed 'bref för 1628')
documents.route: Stockholm -> Axel Oxenstierna in Prussia (from the 1888 print; filed with letters to Ludwig Camerarius)

transcription.notes: Agent transcription of 21 Sept 2026; about 20 multi-digit readings doubtful (possibly two numbers run together); one line written twice in the manuscript. Re-measured 14 Oct 2026 with docs/_check_profile.py --measure: 822 tokens, 170 distinct (the 21 Sept note gave 756 numbers and 108 values; the measure counts every doubtful form as its own value).

system.summary: Numbers separated by commas with Latin words in clear. With the key matched on 25 Oct 2026 (the alphabet strip of DECODE R4325): a homophonic alphabet of 1-108, four numbers per letter, and larger numbers that are probably word codes; the plaintext is Swedish with Latin.
system.notes: A leaf filed with it tries a letter cipher on four phrases (effusorem sanguinis / pestem patriae / praeter naturalem / disturbatorem religionis); not used yet. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from riksarkivet1628 (catalogue 207).

prior_solution.where: Rikskansleren Axel Oxenstiernas skrifter och brefvexling II:1 (1888), no. 296, pp. 362-367: the letter printed from another copy with Lars Grubbe's decipherment of the time (1627); R4284 is the part from p. 366. A parallel text, not a gloss on R4284 (Latin clear words here where the print has Swedish). Found by Andrew Beling (issue #893, Nov 2026), after the key match and the decode of 25-26 Oct 2026.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the 14 DECODE records of catalogue 207 with the project cookie; R4284 (Chifferklaver låda II:114, docketed with the letters to L. Camerarius for 1628) is one of four unrelated groups.
Agent transcription of R4284 (756 numbers, 108 distinct; about 20 doubtful multi-digit readings).
Homophonic Latin annealing of R4284 (8 x 250k), also over 4-number bands.
Fetched 70 Chifferklaver låda II key records (R4259-R4329); tested the Siebenbürgen key (R4310) and the 1632 word-end-30 key (R4296) on R4284 (and R4306): no fit.

Split from the former catalogue-207 group entry riksarkivet1628 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026); R4284 is a cipher of its own. Transcription re-measured (822 tokens, 170 distinct). No new attack.

Dolly Moulekhi (issue #98) tested the Chifferklaver key records against the 21 Sept transcription and found that the horizontal alphabet strip of R4325 (I25940, below the first square grid) gives Swedish and Latin; literal decode of all 41 numerical lines, with her own review of the transcription on the images.

Strip checked here on the R4325 image (PDF rendered at 400 dpi): all 104 values agree with her transcription, 22/51/74/89 unused, Y and Z share a column. docs/_validate.py on her reviewed decode (sv-modern): reading -3.123, shuffled refit -3.342 (best -3.217, z 2.4), random keys -6.458, power -2.996: underdetermined. The decode reads as 17th-century Swedish with enciphered Latin (Östersiön, hamnar, negociera, arfwingar).

Andrew Beling (issue #893, with AI agents) identified the letter in print: Rikskansleren Axel Oxenstiernas skrifter och brefvexling II:1 (1888), no. 296, pp. 362-367, Gustav II Adolf to Axel Oxenstierna, Stockholm, 18 Nov 1627, with Lars Grubbe's decipherment of the time; R4284 is the part from p. 366, in another copy. Checked in the integration review against the Internet Archive OCR text of the volume (not its page images). Title and date corrected from 'Latin letter of 1628'. From the print he proposes ten code values (952 armeens, 831 tollerne, 1493? stilleståndh, 692 twice Polacken/Pollniske, 608 and 1302 Ligisterna(s), 706 Pryssen, 487 assecurera, 1273 konungar): recorded as probable, print only. His segmented reading (Moulekhi's key, no image checked, not in the repository) has 105 of 168 words sure (62.5%) by his strict count, every sentence with a hole; 92 same, 23 equivalent, 5 wrong of the 120 sure words with a counterpart in the print. Three one-digit guesses (208 as 108; line 40, 26 as 36; line 41, 30 and 104 as 36 and 101) are recorded as points to check on the image. Class unchanged: decoded, not read.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 728 tokens, 83 types, sv-modern order 4: reading -3.123 per letter; random keys -6.458 (z 8.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.217 (mean -3.342, z 2.4); annealer on the real text -2.996. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -3.123; polyphony 0.0; 51 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.996
